title: Capacity crosswalk — one-off tracker (May 2027)
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, ad-hoc crosswalk used to reconcile short-term capacity gaps across teams while we triage the customer-impacting routing incident from 2027-05-11. The sheet is intentionally informal — use it for fast updates, not for long-term source-of-truth.

How to use:
- Owner (Maya) maintains the master copy.
- Each row is a discrete mitigation task or observation.
- Update Status and Due date when you change work. If you lower Severity, add a short note.
- Use the linked JIRA keys for follow-ups and mark them in the JIRA ticket when resolved.

Quick summary (human-readable table):
Columns: ID | Item | Owner | Area | Severity(1-5) | Immediate action | Status | Due | Notes / Jira
1 | Regional burst on eu-west-1 serving pool — spike in short-sequence chat traffic | Leo Nguyen | Serving-runtime | 4 | Temporarily scale dedicated pools + divert non-critical routes to us-east fallback | in_progress | 2027-05-14 | JIRA:INF-4231; scaling script applied 05-12 21:00, monitoring 2h window
2 | High embedding queue backlog for embeddings-west | Priya Kapoor | Dedicated / Routing | 3 | Increase concurrency cap for embeddings-worker-03, add warmup pods | todo | 2027-05-15 | Observed 3x baseline latency; potential QoS impact for search reranks
3 | Cache eviction pattern causing cold-starts for long-context models | Aaron Patel | Serving-runtime / Caching | 3 | Adjust prefix caching TTLs and enable aggressive prefetch for active customer keys | in_review | 2027-05-16 | Test run shows 20% fewer cold tokens, need approval from infra
4 | Customer A (enterprise) reporting timeouts on private deployment during peak test feed | Sofia Martinez | Private-deployments / SRE | 5 | Swap to reserve instances, capture packet dump, escalate to PS | escalated | 2027-05-14 | Contacted account exec; PS pinged; JIRA:PS-2107
5 | Observability dashboard alerting gap (missing token-level cost breakdown for dedicated) | Maya Chen | Observability | 2 | Quick instrumentation patch + dashboard refresh | done | 2027-05-13 | Patch rolled to staging; prod rollout scheduled after smoke test
6 | Rollout config mismatch for A/B traffic splitting on rollouts route | Leo Nguyen | Console / Rollouts | 4 | Revert canary to previous stable config; re-run split job | in_progress | 2027-05-14 | Caused 7% extra traffic to new model variant during spike
7 | License/infra billing spike flagged for dedicated GPU pool (unexpected) | Finance escalation | Finance & Infra | 3 | Run usage attribution report; hold non-critical batch jobs | todo | 2027-05-17 | Preliminary cost estimate ~USD 18k extra/day if unmitigated
8 | Quick doc: customer-facing status blurb refresh for status.redwood.ai | Maya Chen | Customer-success / Comms | 1 | Draft and publish short blurb, link to PS ticket | todo | 2027-05-14 | Draft ready, waiting for SRE confirmation on mitigation

Totals (live counts):
- Open rows: 8
- In Progress: 3
- Escalated / High severity (4-5): 4
- Completed: 1

Notes / context (freeform):
- This tracker was created following an unexpected routing pressure event on 2027-05-11 that exposed a few brittle defaults in our automatic fallback rules. Primary failure mode: prefix cache churn + aggressive canary split that increased variance in tail latencies.
- We prioritised customer-facing timeouts and private deployments first (rows 4,1,6). We deferred lower-severity analytics and billing items to separate follow-ups.
- Quick mitigations are intentionally conservative: prefer capacity/route fallbacks over experimental perf optimizations during incidents.

Open questions / blockers:
- Infra needs signoff on cost hold for dedicated batch jobs (Finance flagged). Who on infra will approve? (Action: @Leo to chase)
- Does Private Deployments have a fallback playbook for multi-tenant test feeds? (Action: @Sofia to attach playbook)
- Observability patch requires a rolling restart window — conflict with canary rollback schedule on 2027-05-14 evening. Need alignment.

Next steps & owners (short):
- Leo: finish eu-west scaling + validate tail p95 (due 2027-05-14).
- Sofia: PS escalation loop + customer comms update (due 2027-05-14).
- Aaron: finalize cache TTL test and PR for infra review (due 2027-05-16).
- Priya: spin additional embeddings concurrency and monitor queue depth (due 2027-05-15).
- Maya: publish status blurb and coordinate post-mortem note (due 2027-05-18).

Scratch / quick todos (notes to self):
- Add link to runbook: CONFLUENCE: Runbook-IncidentRouting-v2 (deferred).
- Capture spike sample logs and upload to shared S3 bucket path /incidents/may11/leo.
- After stabilised: run cost delta analysis for dedicated pool scaling (Aaron + Finance).

Minimal retrospective prompts to capture when incident is cold:
- What config allowed the canary to accept extra traffic? (owner: Console team)
- How did caching TTL interplay with request batching? (owner: Serving-runtime)
- What quick wins reduced tail latency most (quantitative)? (owner: Observability)

This sheet is intentionally ephemeral. Once all rows are closed, nominate a single ticket (JIRA) to carry the long-lived follow-ups into product/infrastructure backlog.

Last updated by Maya Chen on 2027-05-14 18:42 UTC.
